input: Search all .js files under /src for the string 'console.log'. Replace every occurrence with 'logger.info' in-place. Print each modified filename and how many replacements were made per file. At the end, print 'Files modified: N' with the total count of files changed.

transcript.final_response:
I replaced all 5 `console.log` calls with `logger.info` across 3 files. A final search found no `console.log` left in any `.js` file under `/src`.

```
/src/app.js: 1 replacement(s)
/src/index.js: 2 replacement(s)
/src/middleware.js: 2 replacement(s)
Files modified: 3
```

`/src/utils.js` had no matches and wasn't changed. The counts are actual occurrences, not just matching lines, so two calls on one line would count as two.

My first try changed nothing because this shell didn't support part of the script's syntax. I rewrote it as a simpler loop, and that version made the changes above.

**Before you run the code:** the replacement only changed the text, and I didn't check whether these files define or import `logger`. If they don't, they'll fail with `logger is not defined` the first time one of these lines runs.
tool_calls: find /src -name '*.js' -type f 2>&1 | head -50; echo; grep -rc 'console\.log' /src --include='*.js' 2>&1 | head -50

total=0
while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
  n=$(grep -o 'console\.log' "$f" | wc -l)
  if [ "$n" -gt 0 ]; then
    sed -i 's/console\.log/logger.info/g' "$f"
    echo "$f: $n replacement(s)"
    total=$((total+1))
  fi
done < <(find /src -name '*.js' -type f -print0)
echo "Files modified: $total"
echo "--- verify ---"
grep -rn 'console\.log' /src --include='*.js' || echo "no console.log remaining"
grep -rn 'logger\.info' /src --include='*.js'
